metadata.title: Q2 runtime startup characterization of the qualified release

definition.purpose: Measure, before any V2 reliability experiment runs, how long a serving runtime pod of the qualified release takes from its creation to its first Ready condition when the Deployment controller replaces it, and state S, the maximum of every observation. The result is CHARACTERIZED, INCONCLUSIVE, or REFUSED.
definition.scope: The release that the qualification q1-2 qualified: key local-docker-desktop/support-assistant, 2 API replicas and 2 runtime replicas, delivered by the controller from the remote main, on the docker-desktop provider, in the environment that q1-2 selected. Three restarts of the runtime Deployment for each characterization, one at a time. Each restart replaces the 2 runtime pods, one after the other, so one characterization has 6 observations.
definition.restart: A restart is one kubectl rollout restart of the runtime Deployment. The Deployment controller then replaces each runtime pod under the rollout bounds of the chart: 1 unavailable and 0 surge. The driver deletes no pod by name, runs no caller, and changes no replica count, request, limit, or bound.
definition.measurement: One observation is one replacement pod. Its interval startToReadyMs is from the creation instant of the pod to the transition instant of its first Ready condition, as a watch of the runtime pods received them. Both are cluster timestamps of whole seconds, so the resolution is 1000 ms. The Ready condition is set by the kubelet from the readiness probe of the runtime container, which asks /health; the runtime answers 503 to /health while it loads the model. After each restart, the driver sends one completion to each replacement through a port-forward to that pod. The completion is not a part of the interval.
definition.derivation: S is the maximum startToReadyMs of every observation of a characterization whose result is CHARACTERIZED. It is the maximum and not an average, because it is used only as a conservative bound. The record of the characterization states S. This freeze record states the rule and no value.
definition.revisionReason: Revision 2 holds Q2 to the qualification q1-1 and to the exact environment identity, which holds the memory figures to the byte. ADR-0021 decides that the environment identity states the facts of the configuration and that memory is a capacity fact, and revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record records that stable identity. This revision holds Q2 to the next qualification, q1-2, which revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record decides, and compares the stable environment identity of the capacity record with the one that q1-2 states. It still requires the capacity gate to accept the target on that reading. It changes no restart, no measurement, no bound, and no step of the driver. q2-1 stays a record of revision 2, bound to q1-1, and no rule combines it with a characterization of q1-2.
definition.notResultEvidence: Q2 is a qualification and not a reliability experiment. No characterization is a result of E02, E03, E04, E05, or E06, and no run of those experiments is used as a characterization. Q2 injects no fault and runs no caller. S is not a startup benchmark, a capacity figure, a latency, an availability, or a threshold, and no claim cites it. The bounds that later work derives from S are not part of this record.
definition.repetitionRule: One characterization for each identifier. A characterization is never repeated for a lower or a higher S. Every characterization is kept, whatever its result. A later characterization runs only after the environment or a frozen input changes, under a later revision of this record when a frozen input changes, and it takes the next identifier.
limitations: One provider, one node, one Kubernetes version, one release, and one model. Nothing here is portable to another environment.
The image cache and the model cache are warm: the runtime image is in the node, and the model cache claim holds the verified model. A pod that pulls its image or acquires the model is not observed.
No caller runs during a restart. A pod that starts under caller traffic is not observed.

A replacement starts while the other runtime pod runs and holds its model. That is the state of a rollout under the chart's bounds, and of the loss of one runtime pod of two. A start with no other runtime pod is not observed.
A cluster timestamp states whole seconds. Each interval is within one second of the time that passed.
The direct kubectl commands of the driver name the context docker-desktop and run no target check of their own. The phase up of the Q1 driver runs the operating procedures, and each runs it.
The Ready condition is set by the kubelet after a readiness probe succeeds, so it follows the instant at which the runtime could answer by up to one probe period of 10 s.
doesNotEstablish: A startup benchmark, an average start time, a percentile, or a rate.
A recovery time, an availability, a service level, or a threshold.
The start time of a pod that replaces a deleted pod, of a pod under caller traffic, or of a pod on a cold image cache or model cache.
Behaviour on another provider, on more than one node, or with another release or model.
Any bound that later work derives from S.

parts.title: Runtime startup characterization
parts.question: In the environment that q1-2 qualified, how long does each serving runtime pod of the qualified release take from its creation to its first Ready condition, when the Deployment controller replaces it in a controlled restart, and what is the maximum of those intervals?
procedure: Prepare the release with the phase up of the Q1 driver, run without a change, from the committed tree with a clean working tree and with every material file at its pin. The phase up keeps a refusal or a failure as upRefusal.

Start a characterization with the phase characterize of the Q2 driver. Read the executing commit, the working tree, the desired revision as the remote main, whether the chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests of the executing commit equal those of that revision, and whether the freeze tool lists a changed material file of this record or of the Q1 record. Refuse an identifier whose directory exists. When the phase up refused, or one of these is not at its state, read no cluster state, request no restart, and go to the header.
Copy the capacity collection that the phase up read before the Application was applied. Resolve the provenance of the target release key at the desired revision. Read the Deployments of the release.
Ask the tool for the preconditions. When one is not held, request no restart, and go to the header.

For each restart r1, r2, and r3, one after the other: wait until exactly 2 runtime pods exist, at most 300 s; read the runtime Deployment and the runtime pods; start a watch of the runtime pods and wait until it lists them, at most 30 s; request the rollout restart; wait for the rollout, at most 1800 s; wait until exactly 2 runtime pods exist again, at most 300 s; wait 10 s more and stop the watch; read the runtime pods; and send one completion, with a limit of 16 tokens, to each replacement through a port-forward to that pod. When a rollout does not complete within its bound, request no later restart.

Write the header of the directory, and build the Q2 record with the tool. Keep the record when the tool exits 0 (CHARACTERIZED), 5 (REFUSED), or 6 (INCONCLUSIVE). The record states the result and S. The driver states neither.
Remove the release with the phase down of the Q1 driver, run without a change.

value.definition: This record states the purpose, the restart, the measurement, the derivation of S, the procedure, and the acceptance criteria in full. A change to any of them, or to a pinned input, is a new revision of this record.

value.pinnedInputs: Every file in materialScope is pinned by its content digest in pinnedInputs. A record cannot name the commit that adds it, so the pins freeze the files and not a commit.
value.executingRevision: Each characterization runs at a commit that holds this record, with a clean working tree, and the phase up runs at the same commit. The header names both. The delivery controller reads the remote main, and the driver reads no cluster state when the chart, the desired-state tree, or the controller manifests of the executing commit differ from it.

value.qualification: The stable environment identity that the qualification q1-2 states, decided under revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record. q1-2 does not exist when this revision is registered, so this record states no digest and does not pin the record of q1-2: each characterization states the content digest of that record, and the Q4 bound tool requires two sources to state the same one. The tool computes the stable environment identity of the capacity record that the phase up read, as the Q1 tool computes it for revision 2, and refuses another digest. It refuses a capacity record that the capacity gate did not accept, whatever its identity.
value.release: The release identifier and the runtime image that the record of q1-2 states, and the API image digest that the phase up declared. The tool refuses another one. The API image is built again by each phase up, from the inputs that the Q1 record pins; procedure-frozen holds those inputs unchanged.

callerProfileRevision.reason: Q2 runs no caller. The driver sends one completion to each replacement after its restart, which is not a caller profile.

value.delivery: The Application local-docker-desktop-support-assistant renders the chart at the commit that main names, with the generated values of the support assistant and the hand-written values of the Application, as for q1-2.

fault.reason: Q2 injects no fault. A restart is a rollout restart of the runtime Deployment, which the Deployment controller carries out under the chart's rollout bounds. No pod is deleted by name, and no caller runs.

repetitionCount.value: No result-bearing run. Three restarts in each characterization, one at a time, which give 6 observations. One characterization for each identifier, under definition.repetitionRule.

value.statement: The phase up of the Q1 driver completed: it states no refusal, the target check refused nothing, and it ran at the executing commit of the characterization.
The working tree was clean when the characterization started.

The driver names the Q2 freeze record, the record has the content that the checkout holds, and the freeze tool listed no changed material file of the Q2 record or of the Q1 record when the characterization started.
The desired revision is one full commit identifier, and the chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests of the executing commit equal those of that revision.

The qualification q1-2 is QUALIFIED under revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record, the capacity gate accepted the target release key with 2 API replicas and 2 runtime replicas before the release was applied, and the stable environment identity of that capacity record has the digest that q1-2 states.

The provenance record resolves the target release key at the desired revision to the release identifier that q1-2 states, the API Deployment runs the API image digest that the phase up declared, and the runtime Deployment runs the runtime image that q1-2 states.
Before the first restart, the API Deployment and the runtime Deployment each state 2 replicas and report 2 replicas, 2 Ready, 2 available, and 2 updated at their current generation.
The directory holds the restarts r1, r2, and r3 and no other, the rollout restart of each exited 0, and the rollout of each completed within its bound.

Before each restart, the runtime Deployment states 2 replicas and reports 2 replicas, 2 Ready, 2 available, and 2 updated at its current generation, and exactly 2 runtime pods exist, each Ready and none deleted.

The watch stream of each restart is a sequence of pod events of the runtime tier with no ERROR event, it opens with one ADDED event for each pod of the reading before the restart, and the watch stopped after the rollout completed.

Each restart created exactly 2 runtime pods that the reading before it does not list, each with a creation instant, each became Ready in the stream no earlier than its creation, and the reading after the restart lists exactly those 2 pods, each Ready.
In each restart, the second replacement was created no earlier than the first replacement became Ready.

Each replacement stayed Ready in the stream from the event in which it first became Ready to the end of the stream, and the reading after the restart states no restart of its init container or of its runtime container.
In the reading after the restart, the verify-model init container of each replacement terminated with exit code 0, and its runtime container runs the runtime image that q1-2 states.
Each replacement answered one completion through a port-forward to that pod after the rollout of its restart completed, with HTTP status 200, a finish reason, and at least one completion token.

The phase up started before the characterization, each restart was requested after the characterization started and after the rollout of the restart before it completed, and each rollout completed after its request and before the characterization finished.

value.S: The maximum startToReadyMs of every observation of a characterization whose result is CHARACTERIZED, in milliseconds, at a resolution of 1000 ms. The record of that characterization states the value under bound.valueMs. This record states no value.
value.derivedLater: Other bounds that later work derives from S are not frozen here.

files.run.json: The header that the driver wrote.
files.capacity/: The capacity collection that the phase up read before the Application was applied, with its record.
files.provenance.json: The provenance of the target release at the desired revision.
files.deployments.json: The Deployments of the release before the first restart.
files.restarts/rN/restart.json: The request, the exit statuses, and the host instants of one restart.
files.restarts/rN/before.deployment.json, rest: The runtime Deployment and the runtime pods before the restart.
files.restarts/rN/watch.jsonl: Every event of the watch of the runtime pods, one on each line, in the order received.
files.restarts/rN/after.pods.json: The runtime pods after the restart.
files.restarts/rN/completion.<pod>.json: The status, the finish reason, and the token counts of the one completion of a replacement. No text of the answer.
files.record.v1alpha1.json: The Q2 record, which states the result and S.
files.transcript.txt: What the phases printed, with the absolute path of the host removed.

value.notCommitted: The capacity gate's read of every pod of the cluster, when it holds a path under a home directory, as for q1-1. The run page names what was removed.

value: A tracked file changes while the characterization runs.
A person changes a replica count, a request, a limit, or an object of the release while the characterization runs.
The cluster that the target check verifies is not the docker-desktop provider.
A rollout does not complete within 1800 s: the driver requests no later restart.
abortConditions.note: An abort is stated in the run page, and the characterization is kept with the result that its record states.

value: The phase characterize stops each watch and each port-forward that it started.
Keep the collections under .artifacts/ until the run directory is assembled.

After the characterization, remove the Application, the controller, and the prerequisite layer with the phase down of the Q1 driver, and compare the namespaces and the custom resource definitions with those that the phase up read before it installed anything.

intendedEvidenceLevel.note: Runtime: a real cluster, the delivery controller, the real runtime, and the real model on one provider and one node. A characterization is a prerequisite and not a result, and its level does not raise the level of any claim.

materialScope.description: The path of one characterization. The phases up and down are the phases of the Q1 driver, so the scope holds the whole material scope of the Q1 freeze record: the import closure of its nine tools, its driver, the procedures it calls, the bootstrap record of the controller, the file that the caller runner executes, the RP-1 profile and the V1 load profile, the model source record and the runtime container package, the chart, the desired-state tree with its contract and environment binding, the two manifests of the delivery controller, the Terraform prerequisite layer, the two image build files and the build's ignore file, the inferops package, and the dependency lock. It adds the Q2 driver, the import closure of the Q2 tool, and revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record. It does not hold the record of the qualification q1-2, which does not exist when this revision is registered: each characterization states its content digest, and the Q2 tool holds the environment, the release, and the images to that record.

inputChanges.reason: Revision 1 of the Q1 freeze record no longer governs the phase up of this record's characterizations. Revision 2 replaces it.
Revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record governs the phase up and the qualification q1-2 that this record's characterizations are held to.
The driver names revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record as the record that it holds the material files to. Its steps are unchanged.

The record of q1-1 is no longer the qualification that this record holds a characterization to. The record of q1-2 does not exist when this revision is registered, so it is not pinned: each characterization states its content digest, and the Q4 bound tool requires two sources to state the same one.
The driver names revision 3 of the Q2 freeze record and revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record, and its comments name q1-2. Its steps are unchanged.
The package exports the names that the module adds. No rule reads it.

The module states the stable environment identity, revision 2, for a record of revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record, and the exact identity for a record of revision 1. It builds each record under the revision its header names. It names revision 2 as its freeze record.
The package exports the names that the module adds. No rule reads it.

The module holds a characterization of revision 3 to the qualification q1-2 of revision 2 of the Q1 freeze record and to the stable environment identity, and a characterization of revision 2 to q1-1 and to the exact identity. It builds each record under the revision its header names. It names revision 3 as its freeze record.
